articles.title: I Built a Phone-First Coding Agent in Five Days, on Infrastructure That Costs Nothing
articles.excerpt: Coding agents changed what a working session looks like. You describe the work, and it happens without you. You can walk away for twenty minutes and come back to a finished change. The tools around th…
articles.body: Coding agents changed what a working session looks like. You describe the work, and it happens without you. You can walk away for twenty minutes and come back to a finished change. The tools around them haven't caught up. Almost all of them still assume you're sitting at the machine the agent runs on, watching it. I often wasn't. Some days I was nowhere near my PC, and on others I was near it but couldn't do any real work on it. Long-running agents looked like the obvious answer: start the work, walk away, let it run. What I wanted was a way to hand work to an agent while my PC was off. That raised two questions right away. If I'm away for hours, how do I keep the agent's output good enough to be worth keeping?
articles.author: MrSuperCraft

articles.title: Idea Board — Turn 3 AM Idea Overload into Actionable 30-Minute Tasks with Local AI
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend I built Idea Board for my best friend who suffers from severe "3 AM idea overload." He constantly wakes up with ambitio…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend What I Built I built Idea Board for my best friend who suffers from severe "3 AM idea overload." He constantly wakes up with ambitious side-project ideas, writes down vague goals like "Learn AI vectors" or "Build a search engine," but gets completely overwhelmed trying to figure out where to start. Within a few days, those ideas die in his notes app clutter. Idea Board solves this by converting any vague goal or project idea into a structured, step-by-step Kanban task board in seconds. Each generated task is concrete, starts with an action verb, and is strictly capped at 15 to 60 minutes so he can make real progress in bite-sized sessions without feeling overwhelmed.
articles.author: Vijay Kumar

Most AI tools hand over the answer, and my friend ended up copy-pasting code without understanding it. Byte-Gemma is a fine-tuned Gemma 3 1B that teaches Socratically. It stays under ~100 words, praises one thing you got right, and asks one guiding question. It runs locally on Android, so it works without internet or an API bill.

articles.title: Building CyberRef: A Single-Binary Offline Reference for Cybersecurity Practitioners
articles.excerpt: I built CyberRef to solve a problem I kept seeing in labs and on engagements: nobody remembers the exact syntax of a command under pressure. You know the command exists. You know roughly what it does.…
articles.body: I built CyberRef to solve a problem I kept seeing in labs and on engagements: nobody remembers the exact syntax of a command under pressure. You know the command exists. You know roughly what it does. But it's 2 AM during an incident, or you're mid-engagement with a client watching, and the exact flags slip away. So you open twelve tabs of cheatsheets, dig through your notes app, ask Slack — and twenty minutes disappear on something you knew cold last week. CyberRef is my attempt to fix that. This article is a walkthrough of what it does, the design decisions behind it, and what I learned building it. What It Is A single binary you download and run. It opens a local web UI at http://localhost:8787 with a searchable command reference and a set of guided lab scenarios. No install.
articles.author: Elijah Abolaji M.N.C.S

articles.title: My Friend Can't Explain Loglan Grammar Fast Enough — So I Built Him an AI That Speaks a 1955 Artificial Language
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend Meet Alex — one of a small handful of mentors who keep Loglan alive. Loglan (Logical Language) was invented in 1955 by…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend The Friend Meet Alex — one of a small handful of mentors who keep Loglan alive. Loglan (Logical Language) was invented in 1955 by Dr. James Cooke Brown to test the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis: does the structure of a language shape how its speakers think? Brown's answer was radical: build a language from scratch with a strict mathematical guarantee that no natural language possesses. Every grammatically valid Loglan sentence has exactly one parse tree. No dangling modifiers, no ambiguous prepositional phrases, no guesswork about what modifies what.
articles.author: torrua

articles.title: HearthLore - Preserving the Recipes, Voices & Stories of Home
articles.excerpt: HearthLore: Preserving the Recipes, Voices, and Stories of Home This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend. HearthLore is an AI-powered family recipe and oral his…
articles.body: HearthLore: Preserving the Recipes, Voices, and Stories of Home This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend. What I Built HearthLore is an AI-powered family recipe and oral history preservation app built for the people in our lives whose best dishes exist only in memory, voice notes, and casual conversations rather than neat cookbooks. Think of that one relative who explains a dish with phrases like: "Bas thoda sa daalna hai... jab tak khushboo na aaye tab tak pakao." Everyone at the table knows exactly what that tastes like, but nobody actually has the measurements written down. The instructions rely on intuition and aroma, and the stories tied to those meals risk being lost when the person who cooks them is no longer around.

articles.body: Marvel Studios' Encore re-release has helped Avengers: Endgame beat Avatar to become the highest-grossing movie at the box office of all time…again. Despite not cracking the top five earners for this weekend's box office returns, Avengers: Endgame Encore managed to scrounge together enough cash to reach a total of $2.9255 billion worldwide. It's a number that essentially puts it just a few bucks over Avatar's standing total of $2.9237 billion, securing the Marvel movie's place as the movie to make the most in theaters. articles.title: The Soulog Sense is an AI voice recorder with a personal context system that never misses a word
articles.excerpt: It not only records your conversations, but it also helps you understand and organize them.
articles.body: Credit: SOULOG Plenty of important details get said out loud once and never written down: a price quoted on a call, a delivery date mentioned as a meeting wraps up, the name of a tool a colleague recommends in passing. In a week full of calls, meetings, and classes, most of them are gone by the time you need them. A standard voice recorder certainly helps, but it leaves you with hours of audio and transcripts to dig through, with nothing linking the words to the files, photos, and earlier conversations around them. The Soulog Sense , paired with the Soulog app, not only records and transcribes the conversation but also sorts it by topic and decision and connects it to the surrounding material, so you can search it, revisit it, and build on it later. Here’s what you need to know.

articles.excerpt: Buffy the Vampire Slayer ran for seven seasons, but cutting two of its weakest would have made the beloved series even better.
articles.body: It's difficult to overstate the influence of Buffy the Vampire Slayer . The TV show (1997-2003) was never a ratings giant, but it was a hit with critics and quickly developed a fanatical fan following. We can credit and/or blame Buffy for TV Tropes , some significant fraction of urban fantasy as a genre, a surprising amount of modern media-discussion slang (i.e. "big bad"), and the Marvel Cinematic Universe. If you were going to build a Mount Rushmore for Western pop culture, Buffy Summers is on the short list.

articles.excerpt: The engineering development unit for NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) probe is photographed prior to a major thermal evaluation. The DAVINCI…
articles.body: An engineering model of NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) descent probe passed a key test that ran from Aug. 28 to Sept. 10, showing it can survive the extreme temperatures of Venus. NASA/Mike Guinto The engineering development unit for NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) probe is photographed prior to a major thermal evaluation. The DAVINCI team put the yoga ball-sized vessel into a ceramic-lined chamber with heat-scorched walls and ratcheted up the temperature to 869 F, or 465 C, over the course of about an hour — the same pace the probe will heat up during its descent to the surface of Venus.
